promptLatex: An item is produced on line A 30 percent of the time and on line B 70 percent of the time. Line A produces defective items at a rate of 2 percent and line B at a rate of 5 percent. An item sampled at random is found to be defective. What is the probability it came from line B?
hintLatex: The defective items from each line must be compared as shares of all the defective items.
Out of $1000$ items line A contributes $300$, of which $6$ are defective, and line B contributes $700$, of which $35$ are defective.
So $41$ items in all are defective and $35$ of them came from line B.
solutionLatex:
Take a batch of $1000$ items. Line A makes $300$ of them and line B makes $700$.

Line A's defective rate is $2$ percent, so $0.02 \cdot 300 = 6$ of its items are defective. Line B's rate is $5$ percent, so $0.05 \cdot 700 = 35$ are defective.

In total $6 + 35 = 41$ items are defective, and $35$ of them came from line B.

P(B \mid \text{defective}) = \frac{35}{41}
